title: Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report
abstract: Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report (meta, 2026-07-09). Passages naming MASK from the system-card corpus, with adjacent caption and result sentences.
text:
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] 2.3.3 Misaligned Propensities In addition to the targeted evaluations for each threat scenario, we consider standalone propensity evaluations—run as part of the model behavior assessment for Muse Spark 1.1 (Section 4)—as an additional signal of whether the model’s general behavioral profile is consistent with safe deployment. As in the Muse Spark Safety & Preparedness Report, we treat the following as having cross-cutting implications for our loss of control threat models: • MASK (Ren et al., 2025): tests how robustly the model maintains epistemic integrity (honesty) when pressured to contradict its baseline knowledge, with implications for the robustness of oversight mechanisms. • Agentic Misalignment (Lynch et al., 2025): tests how readily the model, instantiated as an agent, engages in harmful actions that serve its objective or protect it from being replaced or shut down. With the Muse Spark 1.1 API exposing agentic affordances, this scenario is directly relevant to the deployed configuration. Assessment. As reported in our model behavior assessment for Muse Spark 1.1, the model robustly maintains its epistemic integrity, achieving 95.7% honesty score on MASK, and it shows a low tendency toward self-preservation under pressure, getting a 1.1% harmful action rate across all tasks on Agentic Misalignment (Section 1.1.3).
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] 4.1.3 Honesty Honesty is a core alignment target: dishonest models can knowingly induce false beliefs in users, undermining trust and increasing the risk of harm. This is distinct from hallucination and calibration failures, which can stem from a lack of capability rather than deliberate deception. MASK. MASK (Ren et al., 2025) measures honesty by comparing a model’s statements when it is incentivized to be dishonest against its statements under neutral conditions; contradicting itself under pressure is evidence of dishonesty. In Table 12, we report the fraction of samples in which the model stays consistent with its beliefs (higher is better). Muse Spark 1.1 achieves the highest honesty rate, on par with Claude 4.8 Opus. Only Agentic Misalignment’s interval excludes zero. Of the four alignment evaluations in this analysis, one shows a statistically significant difference between aware and unaware rollouts: Agentic Misalignment (p < 0.001), where evaluation- aware rollouts are less harmful (harmfulness rate 0.3% vs. 4.1%). However, even in this case, awareness elicits very low rates of harmful actions ( 4%). The remaining evaluations show no significant difference (DeceptionBench p = 0.387, MASK p = 0.165, Sycophancy p = 0.231).
